name: WaterFire Providence
unique: Eighty bonfires floating down three rivers through downtown, scored with world music, while a hundred thousand people drift along the banks.
buzz: It is genuinely magical and completely free; reviews warn about crowds and restaurant waits. Arrive by dusk and walk the whole loop.

name: Newport Cliff Walk
unique: A 3.5-mile path squeezed between Gilded Age mansion backyards and a raw Atlantic ledge, with the Breakers rising over the fence at one end.
buzz: Locals call it the best free thing in New England and warn that the southern half is real scrambling, not a boardwalk. Wear grip.

name: Newport Folk Festival
unique: The festival where Dylan went electric, now a curated three day bill at Fort Adams with harbor views and a no-corporate ethos that survived the decades.
buzz: Sound and setting are praised; the fort's lawn is steep and the food lines long. Locals say volunteer or work it if you want the cheap way in.

name: The Breakers
customer: House tour people, architecture fans, families
unique: The Vanderbilt summer cottage of 70 rooms, with a great hall of Caen limestone, a dining room that took a year to carve and a cliff walk terrace over the Atlantic.
buzz: The audio tour is better than the guided one for the details; buy the multi house ticket if you are doing two or three.

name: Block Island Bluffs
unique: Mohegan Bluffs drop 200 feet to a boulder beach, with a 19th century granite lighthouse offshore and 25 miles of empty road to bike.
buzz: The ferry is the bottleneck; book bikes on the island and skip bringing a car. Mansion Beach and the bluffs are the two musts.

name: RISD Museum
unique: A design school museum with a 12th century French chapel, a Mesopotamian lion, Gorham silver and a room of student work, all in a block of College Hill.
buzz: The decorative arts and the costume galleries are quietly excellent; the museum is free on Sundays and students use it as a study hall.

name: Bristol Fourth of July Parade
unique: The oldest continuous Fourth of July celebration in the country, a morning parade down Hope Street past colonial houses with the nation's oldest flag still flying.
buzz: Locals claim their spot the night before; parking is impossible and the walk from the edge of town is part of the ritual.

name: The Steel Yard
unique: An industrial arts center on a former steel site with blacksmithing, welding, ceramics and jewelry classes, plus public art projects made by members.
buzz: The teaching is good and the space is honest; intro welding fills fast.

name: Blithewold Mansion
unique: A 45 room summer mansion on Narragansett Bay with a 10 acre arboretum, a giant sequoia and a bamboo grove, all on a lawn that runs to the water.
buzz: Gardeners come for the rare trees and the spring bulb show; the house tour is short and the grounds are the reason to stay.

name: Herreshoff Marine Museum
customer: Sailors, boat builders, America's Cup fans
unique: The boatyard where Captain Nat Herreshoff built six America's Cup defenders, with a model room, the catamarans of 1988 and a working waterfront.
buzz: Sailing people treat it as a shrine and non sailors are converted by the model room; the restored boats are in the water in summer.

name: International Tennis Hall of Fame
unique: A museum inside the 1880 Newport Casino, with the original grass courts still played on and a gallery of the sport's oddest trophies.
buzz: The grass courts are the surprise; you can book a hit after the museum. The building alone is worth the ticket.

name: Benefit Street Mile of History
unique: A mile of original colonial and federal houses on College Hill, with the First Baptist Church in America at one end and a burial ground where Roger Williams is remembered.
buzz: The street itself is free and the best architecture walk in the state; the Athenaeum and the John Brown House are the paid stops.

name: Federal Hill Food Crawl
company: Self guided or Rhode Island Red Food Tours
unique: Atwells Avenue's Italian-American quarter: strip-mall pastry counters, a century old salumeria and a bakery that sells nothing but pizza strips.
buzz: The consensus is to graze rather than commit to one restaurant; Pastiche for dessert and Tony's Colonial for supplies. Tour guides get warm reviews.

name: Ocean Drive
unique: Ten miles of coastal road past Gilded Age cottages, rocky coves, Brenton Point and the entrance to the Cliff Walk, with the ocean on one side and stone walls on the other.
buzz: Drive it at sunset and stop at Brenton Point; cyclists do the loop in summer and the road is narrow in places.

name: Providence Athenaeum
unique: A subscription library in a Greek revival building with a spiral staircase, gas lamps and the book club that Edgar Allan Poe reviewed for.
buzz: Book people call it one of the most beautiful rooms in New England and visitors are welcome to look; it is still a working library.

name: Roger Williams Park Zoo
unique: A zoo in an Olmsted designed park with a rainforest building, elephants and a carousel, one of the oldest zoos in the country.
buzz: The rainforest and the elephants are the family stops and the park around it has a lake and a botanical center; it is big enough for a half day.

name: Sachuest Point National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A rocky peninsula between the Sakonnet and the Atlantic with trails along the shore, where harlequin ducks winter and monarchs stage in fall.
buzz: The winter waterfowl are the reason birders come and the loop trail is flat; the wind is constant and the paths are gravel.

name: International Yacht Restoration School
company: IYRS School of Technology and Trades
unique: A boatbuilding school on Newport harbor where you can watch students restore wooden yachts and a 1885 schooner in the water.
buzz: The workshop is open to visitors and the smell of varnish is the attraction; it is free and the students will explain what they are doing.

name: Misquamicut State Beach
unique: A wide barrier beach with real surf, a boardwalk of food stands and the Atlantic on one side and a salt pond on the other.
buzz: It is the busiest beach in the state and the surf is the draw; arrive before nine or park in the private lots across the road.

name: Watch Hill Carousel
unique: A flying horse carousel built in 1879 hanging from chains rather than mounted on a frame, still turning beside a Rhode Island beach.
buzz: Collectors say it is one of the oldest in the country; the ride is two dollars and the beach and lighthouse are a short walk.

name: Ninigret National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A former naval airfield turned refuge of salt ponds and grassland where ospreys and herons nest and a bike path runs to the beach.
buzz: The trails and the salt pond are quiet and the bike path connects to the beach; the ticks are bad in summer.

name: East Greenwich Main Street
unique: A hilltop main street of 18th century houses and taverns ending at the harbor, with a view over Narragansett Bay from the bottom of the street.
buzz: Locals come for the restaurants and the water view and the street is small; the Hill and Harbour walk is the local after dinner route.

name: Goddard Memorial State Park
unique: Nearly 500 acres on Greenwich Bay with a beach, a bridle path, a picnic grove and one of the few public polo fields in New England.
buzz: The beach is calm and shallow and the park is quiet on weekdays; the polo matches in summer are free to watch.

name: Nathanael Greene Homestead
customer: Rev war people, history families, locals
unique: The Georgian house Washington's most trusted general built and left to go to war, with period rooms and a forge site on the grounds.
buzz: The volunteers know Greene's campaigns in detail; it is small and only open seasonally, so call before driving.

name: Conimicut Point Park
unique: A sandbar point at the mouth of the Providence River with a view of the Conimicut lighthouse and the bay traffic, a favorite for sitting in the car at dusk.
buzz: Locals come for the sunset and the fishing; the tide comes in fast across the point and there is no lifeguard.
